newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK CREDITANSTALT TURNS TO PROFIT IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK CREDITANSTALT TURNS TO PROFIT IN 1996.

text.p: Creditanstalt a.s., a the Slovak unit of Austrian bank Creditanstalt Bankverein, said on Wednesday it posted a 93.2 million crown net profit in 1996, after a loss of 70.1 million in 1995.
"We consider the results from the second year (1996) of Creditanstalt's operations in Bratislava as excellent," company spokeswoman Svetlana Liskova said.
She said Creditanstalt's balance sheet totalled 8.2 billion crowns as of December 31, 1996, more than double the previous year.
Net interest revenue increased in 1996 by 160 percent to total 153 million crowns, while operational revenues totalled 244.8 million crowns, she added.
Liskova said the bank expects to make further gains in 1997, with a target of a 110 million crown net profit.
"The bank posted a 51 million crown profit in the first quarter of 1997, which indicates it could achieve its full- year plan," she added.
The bank plans to open new operating units in 1997 in Bratislava, Banska Bystrica and the eastern Slovak Kosice, employing some 100 to 110 people in total.
